#!/bin/bash
# Run this script on your server as root or with sudo

set -e

# Create directories
mkdir -p /git/server
mkdir -p /var/www/html

# Initialize bare git repository
cd /git/server
git init --bare

# Create the post-receive hook
cat > /git/server/hooks/post-receive << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Deploy code to web directory on every push

DEPLOY_DIR="/var/www/html"
GIT_DIR="$(pwd)"

# Create a temporary directory for checkout
TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap "rm -rf $TEMP_DIR" EXIT

# Export the pushed branch to the temp directory
git --git-dir=$GIT_DIR --work-tree=$TEMP_DIR checkout -f

# Remove old files and copy new ones
rm -rf $DEPLOY_DIR/*
cp -r $TEMP_DIR/* $DEPLOY_DIR/

# Fix permissions (adjust as needed)
chown -R www-data:www-data $DEPLOY_DIR
chmod -R 755 $DEPLOY_DIR

echo "Deployment complete"
EOF

chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive

echo "✓ Bare git repository created at /git/server"
echo "✓ Post-receive hook installed"

# Git Server Setup Guide

This guide will help you set up a git server with automatic web deployment.

## Architecture

- **Git Server**: Bare repository at `/git/server` with a post-receive hook
- **Web Server**: Nginx serving files from `/var/www/html` on port 8080
- **Deployment**: Automatic on each git push via the post-receive hook

## Server Setup

### Step 1: Set up the Git Repository

Run this on your server:

```bash
sudo bash setup-git-server.sh
```

This creates:
- A bare git repository at `/git/server`
- A post-receive hook that auto-deploys on push

### Step 2: Set up Nginx

Run this on your server:

```bash
sudo bash setup-nginx.sh
```

This installs and configures nginx to serve on port 8080.

## Client Usage

From your local machine, clone and work with the repository:

```bash
# Clone the repository
git clone user@server:/git/server my-project
cd my-project

# Make changes
echo "hello world" > hello.html

# Commit and push
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

## Verify It Works

After pushing, test the deployment:

```bash
# From your local machine
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
# Should output: hello world
```

## How It Works

1. You push to `git@server:/git/server`
2. Git server runs the `post-receive` hook
3. The hook checks out the latest code to `/var/www/html`
4. Nginx serves files from that directory on port 8080

## Troubleshooting

### Check git repository permissions
```bash
sudo ls -la /git/server
sudo ls -la /var/www/html
```

### Check nginx is running
```bash
sudo systemctl status nginx
sudo nginx -t  # Check config syntax
```

### Watch deployment in action
Monitor the git push output to see if the hook executes. If you don't see "Deployment complete", check `/var/www/html` for the files.

### Debug the post-receive hook
Add logging to the hook:
```bash
sudo nano /git/server/hooks/post-receive
# Add: set -x  # For verbose output
```

## Alternative: Using Apache

If you prefer Apache over Nginx, use this config in `/etc/apache2/sites-available/git-server.conf`:

```apache
<VirtualHost *:8080>
    ServerName _
    DocumentRoot /var/www/html
    <Directory /var/www/html>
        Options Indexes FollowSymLinks
        AllowOverride None
        Require all granted
    </Directory>
</VirtualHost>
```

Then enable it:
```bash
sudo a2ensite git-server
sudo a2enmod rewrite
sudo systemctl restart apache2
```

## Notes

- The `www-data` user owns the web directory (created by the post-receive hook)
- SSH access to the git server needs to be configured separately (which you mentioned you'll handle)
- Make sure your user can SSH to the server as specified in the clone URL

#!/bin/bash
# Complete git server + nginx setup in one script
# Run as: sudo bash complete-setup.sh

set -e

echo "=========================================="
echo "Git Server + Nginx Setup"
echo "=========================================="

# Step 1: Install nginx
echo ""
echo "[1/5] Installing nginx..."
if ! command -v nginx &> /dev/null; then
    apt-get update
    apt-get install -y nginx
    echo "✓ Nginx installed"
else
    echo "✓ Nginx already installed"
fi

# Step 2: Create directories
echo ""
echo "[2/5] Creating directories..."
mkdir -p /git/server
mkdir -p /var/www/html
echo "✓ Directories created"

# Step 3: Initialize bare git repository
echo ""
echo "[3/5] Setting up bare git repository..."
cd /git/server
git init --bare
echo "✓ Bare repository initialized at /git/server"

# Step 4: Create and install post-receive hook
echo ""
echo "[4/5] Installing post-receive hook..."
cat > /git/server/hooks/post-receive << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Deploy code to web directory on every push

DEPLOY_DIR="/var/www/html"
GIT_DIR="$(pwd)"

# Create a temporary directory for checkout
TEMP_DIR=$(mktemp -d)
trap "rm -rf $TEMP_DIR" EXIT

# Export the pushed branch to the temp directory
git --git-dir=$GIT_DIR --work-tree=$TEMP_DIR checkout -f

# Remove old files and copy new ones
rm -rf $DEPLOY_DIR/*
cp -r $TEMP_DIR/* $DEPLOY_DIR/ 2>/dev/null || true

# Fix permissions
chown -R www-data:www-data $DEPLOY_DIR
chmod -R 755 $DEPLOY_DIR

echo "✓ Deployment complete"
EOF

chmod +x /git/server/hooks/post-receive
echo "✓ Post-receive hook installed"

# Step 5: Configure nginx
echo ""
echo "[5/5] Configuring nginx..."

# Create nginx config
cat > /etc/nginx/sites-available/git-server << 'EOF'
server {
    listen 8080 default_server;
    listen [::]:8080 default_server;

    server_name _;
    root /var/www/html;

    index index.html index.htm;

    location / {
        try_files $uri $uri/ =404;
    }

    error_page 404 /404.html;
}
EOF

# Enable the site
ln -sf /etc/nginx/sites-available/git-server /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/
rm -f /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/default

# Test and restart
nginx -t
systemctl restart nginx
systemctl enable nginx

echo "✓ Nginx configured on port 8080"

echo ""
echo "=========================================="
echo "Setup Complete!"
echo "=========================================="
echo ""
echo "Your git server is ready at: /git/server"
echo "Web server is running on:    port 8080"
echo "Serving files from:          /var/www/html"
echo ""
echo "Next steps:"
echo "1. Clone the repo on your local machine:"
echo "   git clone user@server:/git/server my-project"
echo ""
echo "2. Make changes and push:"
echo "   cd my-project"
echo "   echo 'hello world' > hello.html"
echo "   git add hello.html"
echo "   git commit -m 'add hello.html'"
echo "   git push origin master"
echo ""
echo "3. Access your deployed file:"
echo "   curl http://server:8080/hello.html"
echo ""

Perfect! I've created a complete git server setup with automatic web deployment. Here's what you need to do:

## Quick Start

On your server, run this single command:

```bash
sudo bash complete-setup.sh
```

This will:
1. Install nginx
2. Create the bare git repository at `/git/server`
3. Install a post-receive hook for automatic deployment
4. Configure nginx to serve on port 8080

## How It Works

```
git push origin master
    ↓
Git server receives push
    ↓
post-receive hook runs
    ↓
Files automatically checked out to /var/www/html
    ↓
Nginx serves them on port 8080
```

## Client Usage

Once the server is set up, from your local machine:

```bash
git clone user@server:/git/server my-project
cd my-project
echo "hello world" > hello.html
git add hello.html
git commit -m "add hello.html"
git push origin master
```

Then test it:

```bash
curl http://server:8080/hello.html
# Output: hello world
```

## Files Created

- **complete-setup.sh** — All-in-one setup script (recommended)
- **setup-git-server.sh** — Just the git server setup
- **setup-nginx.sh** — Just the nginx setup
- **nginx-config.conf** — Nginx configuration file
- **GIT-SERVER-SETUP.md** — Detailed documentation with troubleshooting

All scripts are ready to run. Copy them to your server and execute the `complete-setup.sh` as root.
